body_markdown:
# Daily Loop-Model Briefing - 2026-10-20

## Outcome

Nine papers were added, and each reuses a learned block inside one forward pass. Three are
about training and theory of looped Transformers: a scaling law for truncated
backpropagation, a construction that folds chain-of-thought into loops, and a mechanistic
study of what each iteration computes. Three are design papers: hypersphere fixed-point
halting, block-wise recursive sharing, and gated layer-wise upcycling of a pretrained LLM.
The rest carry loops to proteins and graphs, plus a negative result on nested recursion in
HRM, TRM and URM.

Two additions cite Benhao Huang's work.
[Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25646) uses Equilibrium
Reasoners (EqR) as a baseline. It reports EqR's published Mini-ARC numbers, retrains EqR
under its own protocol, and lists EqR in its comparison of recurrent reasoners.
[Truncate or Not?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26030) cites Towards Looped Models Done Right,
Part II as related work, for looped LMs trained with truncated backpropagation and for
fixed-point gradient approximations.

## Added

### Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
[arXiv:2610.26030](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26030)

**TL;DR:** A scaling law over nearly 600 runs shows that, at matched compute, it is better to
backpropagate fully through fewer loops than to truncate backpropagation through more.

- **Setup:** Prelude-recurrent-coda Transformers with 58M to 919M non-embedding parameters,
  trained on FineWeb-Edu with up to 16 forward loops. Model size, tokens, and forward and
  backward loop counts are varied jointly.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Each setting runs T forward loops and backpropagates through the
  last B. A fitted law turns every (T, B) into an effective parameter count with a bounded,
  saturating gain from the shared block.
- **Results:** The fit reaches R² = 0.9992. At matched compute, (4,4) beats (8,2) at every
  size, for example 2.1057 vs 2.1144 loss at 1B. Trained on 8% more tokens, a 344M model
  with two fully trained loops reaches 2.3590 loss, below the 2.3663 of the compute-optimal
  471M non-looped model.
- **Caveat:** Only dense models and validation loss are measured, with no downstream
  tasks, and when model size is free the law slightly favors not looping at all.
- **Why added:** A controlled scaling and optimization study of weight-tied recurrent
  blocks, including looped-vs-untied comparisons.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II (arXiv:2610.06833),
  cited as related work for truncated backpropagation and fixed-point gradient
  approximations.

### Internalizing Chain-of-thought into Looped Transformers
[arXiv:2610.25998](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25998)

**TL;DR:** A constant-bit-size looped Transformer that interpolates between chain-of-thought
and latent thought, cutting both context window and generated tokens by the loop count L.

- **Setup:** Pure theory: simulating time-t, space-s Turing machines through queue machines
  with a sliding-window decoder.
- **Mechanism / Method:** One shared decoder block runs L times per generated token, and
  each iteration executes one queue-machine transition through a per-iteration KV cache.
- **Results:** The context window is O(s(n)/L), and the number of generated tokens is
  O(t(n)·s(n)^{1/k}/L). The construction also holds with softmax attention at constant bit
  size, under the paper's finite-precision kernel.
- **Caveat:** There are no experiments. The input is preloaded into the cache, and that cost
  is excluded from the bounds.
- **Why added:** An expressivity result specific to weight-tied looped Transformers.

### recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
[arXiv:2610.26747](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26747) · Code: [chandar-lab/AMPLIFY (recamplify branch)](https://github.com/chandar-lab/AMPLIFY/tree/recamplify) · Models: [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/chandar-lab/recamplify)

**TL;DR:** A masked protein language model with a weight-tied recurrent core beats a model
more than twice its size on structure tasks, and a learned halting mixture shortens its
recursion.

- **Setup:** The AMPLIFY pretraining recipe on 2T tokens. A (2,10,2) prelude-core-coda model
  with 155M unique parameters is compared with AMPLIFY-120M and AMPLIFY-350M.
- **Mechanism / Method:** The core refines residue-aligned states over an adjustable number
  of cycles, with the input re-injected each cycle. Gated Mixture Recurrence decodes from a
  probability-weighted mixture of visited states, and a learned residual gate controls how
  much of each update is kept.
- **Results:** Fold accuracy is 0.696 vs 0.568, CASP contact precision 0.179 vs 0.146, and
  stability correlation 0.703 vs 0.585 against AMPLIFY-350M. GMR cuts expected effective
  depth from 52 to 33 to 37 layer applications.
- **Caveat:** It trails AMPLIFY-350M on some zero-shot metrics. The depth savings are
  expected cycles, not measured wall-clock time.
- **Why added:** Recurrent-depth pretraining at scale in a new domain, with adaptive halting.

### Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere
[arXiv:2610.25646](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25646) · Code: [arberzela/sfprm](https://github.com/arberzela/sfprm)

**TL;DR:** Moves fixed-point looped reasoning onto the unit hypersphere, so that state
bounds and halting become geometric and convergence can be proved.

- **Setup:** A 6.83M-parameter Transformer backbone on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, Mini-ARC
  and ARC-1, against FPRM, HRM, TRM, EqR and other baselines.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A weight-tied normalized-Transformer block is iterated as a damped
  fixed-point solver. Input injection and damping are geodesic (slerp) moves, and the loop
  halts on a worst-token angular residual.
- **Results:** 96.6% on Sudoku-Extreme (FPRM 94.2%), 87.9% on Maze-Hard (87.0%), and 59.1%
  on Mini-ARC (FPRM 55.0%, EqR published 55.3%). On Maze it halts on 992 of 1000 inputs,
  22 iterations earlier on average.
- **Caveat:** Single seed per run, and the baseline numbers mix published and retrained
  results.
- **Why added:** Convergence-based depth control over a weight-tied block, with a theory
  component.
- **Cites Benhao's work:** Equilibrium Reasoners (Huang, Geng, Kolter) is a baseline, both
  from published Mini-ARC numbers and retrained, and appears in the related-work comparison
  table.

### Nested Shared-Operator Recursion on ARC-AGI-1: An Empirical Study of HRM, TRM and URM
[arXiv:2610.26666](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26666) · Code: [saraneri01/fractal-recursion](https://github.com/saraneri01/fractal-recursion)

**TL;DR:** Adding a nested intermediate state, updated by the same shared operator, to three
recursive reasoners gives no consistent gain on ARC-AGI-1 under a small budget.

- **Setup:** The official HRM, TRM and URM codebases with parameter-matched nested variants,
  trained on a single GPU partition well below the published budgets.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A persistent intermediate state integrates repeated fast-state
  updates through the same operator before the slow state updates.
- **Results:** TRM token accuracy is 59.86 for the baseline vs 58.59 nested, and URM's is
  62.79 vs 62.80 at 120 epochs. Exact pass@1 is zero for every model except one run at
  0.125%.
- **Caveat:** The baselines do not reach their published accuracy, so the test is weak. The
  authors call the hypothesis open.
- **Why added:** A negative result on hierarchical shared-operator recursion.

### UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop
[arXiv:2610.25004](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25004)

**TL;DR:** Loops each selected middle layer of a pretrained LLM locally, with gated residual
writes, and gains past the usual two-loop ceiling.

- **Setup:** Qwen3-4B Base upcycled with SFT on about 13B tokens and evaluated on 20
  benchmarks; also tested on a 7B-total MoE.
- **Mechanism / Method:** The first and last three layers run once, and each middle layer
  repeats R times with shared weights. Per-layer, per-loop sigmoid gates scale the attention
  and MLP residual writes of later loops, and the loop count follows a staged curriculum.
- **Results:** The average rises from 51.90 (non-looped) and 54.60 (ungated loop) to 55.56
  at R=2, 58.07 at R=3 and 58.70 at a natively trained R=4. The MoE improves from 50.98 to
  55.01.
- **Caveat:** Comparisons are at equal parameters, not equal compute, and code is not yet
  released.
- **Why added:** Retrofitting a pretrained untied model into a looped one.

### Block Recursive Transformers for Structured Parameter Sharing
[arXiv:2610.24998](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24998) · Project: [aim-skku.github.io/BRT](https://aim-skku.github.io/BRT/)

**TL;DR:** Loops contiguous blocks of layers in turn, between per-layer repetition and
whole-stack cycling, and improves on both.

- **Setup:** SmolLM-style decoders from 135M to 1.7B parameters trained on FineWeb-Edu, plus
  T5 and ModernBERT studies.
- **Mechanism / Method:** Each block of the core is applied R times before the next one, and
  the first and last layers stay independent.
- **Results:** At 360M with two loops, BRT reaches a 40.20 average with 157M unique
  parameters, vs 39.74 for a 315M vanilla model and 39.76 for middle-cycle sharing. At
  1.7B it scores 41.63 vs 41.33 for middle-cycle sharing.
- **Caveat:** Gains are small, often within half a point, on five benchmarks. The arXiv
  comment states EMNLP Findings 2026 acceptance, which the catalog has not yet verified.
- **Why added:** A loop-topology study of where shared blocks repeat.

### Inside the Loop: A Mechanistic Study of Weight-Tied Transformers on Depth-Bound Algorithmic Tasks
[arXiv:2610.24135](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24135) · Code: [magnus-sesodia/insidetheloop](https://github.com/magnus-sesodia/insidetheloop)

**TL;DR:** On a multi-hop traversal task, looped Transformers learn where untied ones of
equal depth fail, advancing roughly one hop per iteration.

- **Setup:** Directed permutation traversal with known intermediate answers. Looped blocks of
  2 to 16 layers are compared with untied stacks of matched effective depth over five seeds.
- **Mechanism / Method:** A block with learned iteration embeddings is iterated up to 16
  times, then probed with linear probes, the logit lens and activation patching.
- **Results:** A 4-layer block looped 8 times (3.22M parameters) solves the task in 5 of 5
  seeds, while an untied 32-layer model (25.72M) solves it in 0 of 5 at the same learning
  rate. No model with effective depth 8 or less solves it.
- **Caveat:** One synthetic task at small scale. The untied model succeeds with a lower
  learning rate or with intermediate supervision.
- **Why added:** Mechanistic interpretability of weight-tied recurrence, with iso-depth
  controls.

### Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
[arXiv:2610.24112](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24112)

**TL;DR:** Reuses a pretrained GNN processor beyond its training depth to reach larger
graphs, and steers it with a small controller instead of fine-tuning it.

- **Setup:** Synthetic diffusion targets on random geometric graphs, plus chip placement on
  synthetic and MLCAD 2023 netlists.
- **Mechanism / Method:** An encode-process-decode GNN applies one shared processor K times.
  Loop-Freeze-Steer freezes the processor and trains a FiLM controller conditioned on graph
  size and iteration.
- **Results:** On the largest synthetic designs RMSE is 5.30 for Loop-Tune, 5.61 for LFS and
  7.54 for an untied fine-tuned model. LFS trains 0.17M of 5.85M parameters and stays within
  4% of Loop-Tune.
- **Caveat:** Depth extension needs operator-aligned supervision, and the untied control
  differs in both depth and parameter count.
- **Why added:** A shared processor reused for size generalization, with theory and an
  application.

## Catalog update

This run checked one fifth of the existing catalog (71 papers) for publication venue,
official code links and community comment links. Five entries gained the code repository
that the paper itself names:

- [Universal Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819): tensorflow/tensor2tensor.
- [Are Your Reasoning Models Reasoning or Guessing?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10679):
  renrua52/hrm-mechanistic-analysis.
- [Fixed-Point Masked Generative Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31215):
  andreamiele/fp-mgm.
- [Adaptive Recurrent Message Passing for Test Time Computing on Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22462):
  sunjss/AdaR.
- [Loop Dropout](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34218): NUS-HPC-AI-Lab/loop-dropout.

Venues were not changed. A few papers state acceptances in their arXiv comments, but none
could be confirmed against an official venue page today.

## Near misses

- **Dual-Slot** ([2610.25086](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25086)): shifts a looped core's
  second pass to the next token. At inference each token passes through the core once, so
  inclusion waits on the pending scope decision about depth folded into time.
- **P2N** ([2610.25076](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25076)): adds the previous token's
  middle-core output to the current token's core input. Decoding repeats no layer, so this is
  cross-token feedback under the current scope rule.
- **LowNet** ([2610.24941](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24941)): reuses a 24-parameter linear
  wavelet block as a residual-correction loop for Poisson solving. It is closer to a learned
  unrolled solver than a loop model, so it is held for a maintainer decision.
- **ECHO** ([2610.24766](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24766)): reapplies the final layer
  across multi-token-prediction horizons, feeding each next token back in, so the recursion
  runs along the horizon rather than over depth.
- **Recursive token-merging autoencoder**
  ([2610.26695](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26695)): structural recursion over parse trees,
  with no loop-model argument.
- **Recurrent ViT for spacecraft pose** ([2610.25622](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25622)):
  recurrence across the event stream over time, not over depth.
